title: 第18章 镇魔司的手段，您大可放心
novel_title: 镇守魔教圣女？我一天涨一年功力
content_zh:
丙字号过道。

    火把在石壁上跳动，松油燃烧的噼啪声在死寂的走廊里回荡。

    空气中残留着一股淡淡的焦糊味。

    李长风按着腰间的玄铁令牌，布鞋踩在湿滑的青砖上，没有发出半点声响。

    他身后跟着四名全副武装的狱卒，甲胄碰撞声在空旷的过道里回荡。

    陈然低着头，落后李长风半个身位，手里拎着一串沉重的铁钥匙。

    他周身气血沉寂，内力在《龟息功》的运转下，如同枯木顽石。

    李长风在一间空牢房前停下，指尖划过铁栅栏。

    栅栏上的符文暗淡，边缘处有细微的裂纹。

    “昨夜那股动静，就是从这附近传出来的？”

    李长风转过身，看着陈然。

    陈然躬着腰，双手交叠在腹前，声音平稳。

    “回大人，属下昨夜正在值房歇息，只听得一声巨响，震碎了窗户纸。”

    “属下赶来查看时，走廊里全是白烟。”

    李长风盯着陈然看了三息，又看向那几名狱卒。

    狱卒们纷纷低头。

    “丙字号关的都是重犯，若真出了岔子，你我这颗脑袋都保不住。”

    李长风收回手，继续朝前走去。

    “去雷老虎那看看。”

    ……

    重刑牢房。

    雷老虎被四根锁链吊在半空，琵琶骨被铁钩贯穿，暗红色的血顺着脚尖滴落在地。

    他听到脚步声，猛地抬起头。

    “李长风，你这笑面虎，有种就给老子个痛快！”

    雷老虎咆哮着，锁链被拽得哗啦作响。

    李长风站在栅栏外，按着令牌。

    “雷大当家，这天牢的饭菜虽然粗糙，但胜在管够，何必急着寻死？”

    过道尽头传来一阵急促的脚步声。

    林琬领着三名六扇门捕快走来。

    她穿着一身玄色劲装，长发束成高马尾，腰间的长剑随着步伐晃动。

    李长风拱手行礼。

    “林捕头，什么风把你吹到这阴森之地了？”

    林琬停下脚步，目光在牢房内扫了一圈，最后落在陈然身上。

    她脚步顿了一下。

    “是你？”

    陈然抬起头，目光平静，微微躬身。

    “见过林大人。”

    林琬盯着陈然，意识到了什么：

    “我想起来了当初天牢暴动，是你提供的内鬼线索？”

    李长风侧过头，看着陈然。

    陈然低着头，声音不卑不亢。
content_en:
Aisle C.

    Torches danced on the stone walls, and the crackle of burning pine oil echoed in the dead corridor.

    A faint burnt smell lingered in the air.

    Li Changfeng pressed the black iron token on his waist and stepped on the slippery green bricks with his cloth shoes without making any sound.

    Behind him were four heavily armed jailers, and the sound of armor clashing echoed in the empty corridor.

    Chen Ran lowered his head, half a body behind Li Changfeng, holding a bunch of heavy iron keys in his hand.

    The energy and blood all over his body were silent, and his internal energy was like dead wood and stubborn stone under the operation of "Turtle Breathing Technique".

    Li Changfeng stopped in front of an empty cell and ran his fingertips across the iron bars.

    The runes on the fence are dull and have slight cracks around the edges.

    "Did the noise last night come from around here?"

    Li Changfeng turned around and looked at Chen Ran.

    Chen Ran bowed his waist, folded his hands in front of his abdomen, and spoke in a steady voice.

    "Sir, my subordinate was resting in the room last night when he heard a loud noise that shattered the window paper."

    "When my subordinates came to check, the corridor was full of white smoke."

    Li Changfeng stared at Chen Ran for three breaths, then looked at the jailers.

    The jailers bowed their heads.

    "The ones in Category C are all felons. If something goes wrong, you and I won't be able to save our heads."

    Li Changfeng took back his hand and continued walking forward.

    "Go and have a look at Thunder Tiger."

    …

    Heavy punishment cell.

    Thunder Tiger was hung in the air by four chains, his lute bones were pierced by iron hooks, and dark red blood dripped down his toes and fell to the ground.

    He heard footsteps and looked up sharply.

    "Li Changfeng, you smiling tiger, if you have the guts, give me a good time!"

    Thunder Tiger roared, and the chain rattled as it was pulled.

    Li Changfeng stood outside the fence and pressed the token.

    "Master Lei, although the food in Tianlao is rough, it's better to take care of it. Why rush to seek death?"

    There was a rush of footsteps at the end of the aisle.

    Lin Wan came over with three six-door policemen.

    She was wearing a black outfit, her long hair was tied into a high ponytail, and the sword at her waist swayed with her steps.

    Li Changfeng bowed his hands.

    "Captain Lin, what brought you to this gloomy place?"

    Lin Wan stopped and glanced around the cell, finally landing on Chen Ran.

    She paused.

    "Is it you?"

    Chen Ran raised his head, his eyes were calm, and he bowed slightly.

    "I've met Mr. Lin."

    Lin Wan stared at Chen Ran and realized something:

    "I remember the Tianlao riot. Was it you who provided the clues to the mole?"

    Li Changfeng turned his head and looked at Chen Ran.

    Chen Ran lowered his head and his voice was neither humble nor arrogant.
